artworks.title: Laodamia Writing (from Ovid's Heroides)
artworks.description: BnF Français 875: Laodamia at her desk composing the letter to Protesilaus — Ovid’s Heroides XIII in Octavien de Saint-Gelais’s French. The miniature makes the Phylacian widow the speaking subject of grief: husband first ashore at Troy, briefly returned from the dead.

artworks.title: Laodamia
artworks.description: Joy’s Portsmouth canvas isolates the mourning bride of Protesilaus — Victorian pathos for the wife who loved a ghost and a waxen image. Painted in the century that also read Wordsworth’s Laodamia, it is among the few modern pictures that name her alone.

popCulture.title: Heroides XIII (Laodamia to Protesilaus)
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Ovid’s verse letter gives Laodamia her lasting voice — the newly wed wife begging Protesilaus not to be first ashore, then clinging to his shade.

popCulture.title: Laodamia
popCulture.creator: William Wordsworth
popCulture.description: Wordsworth’s poem retells the brief reunion of Laodamia and the ghost of Protesilaus — Romantic English afterlife of Ovid’s Phylacian widow.
